lines.text: A young woman works the front desk without looking up much.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: How many nights?

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: One, hopefully.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Nobody here stays just one night out of luck.
She says it with no hint of a joke. She hands me the key and goes back to her own business before I can ask anything else.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: How are you holding up after last night, Elena?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Bad. Couldn't sleep a wink. Carla... Carla was a quiet girl. She didn't deserve to end up lying next to that basement.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Any idea why she was near the basement at that hour?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: No idea. The basement's always padlocked... only Robert has the key.
She rubs her arms like she's cold. Her fear seems genuine.

topics.displayName: Calmly ask her why she ran that night

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Someone saw you running the night of the scream. The wrong direction.
Her breath catches half a second before she answers.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: I got scared. I just ran, I don't know where, I just ran to get help.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: It's alright. Nobody said you did anything wrong.
She relaxes, barely. Enough that she doesn't shut down completely.

topics.displayName: Press her directly about her running

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: You were seen running the wrong way from the noise that night. What were you running from?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: What did you want me to do? Just stand there and see if I was next?

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Staying to explain it to the police, for starters.
She shuts down instantly. Crosses her arms and her eyes drop to the counter.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: We're done here. Excuse me.

topics.displayName: Ask her about the master keys

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Who has access to every room in the motel?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Only Robert and I have master keys. I use mine for housekeeping, and Robert keeps the spare in his desk.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Could anyone else have gotten into a room without forcing the door?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Impossible. Unless Robert gave someone a key.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Who else has a key to the basement?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Nobody. Just him. Says it's about the generator.
She answers without looking at me, clipped, like someone paying off a debt she never wanted.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Have you ever been down to the basement?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Never. Only Robert. He says the generator's down there, that it's dangerous, that he'd rather handle it himself.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Honestly, I don't even really know what's down there. And I've worked here two years already.
There's something odd in how she says it. Not suspicion yet. Something older, more tired — like she's only now asking herself why she never asked.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: You again?
She says it without any edge this time. Almost relieved to have someone to talk to.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Sometimes Robert says things. Half joking, half not. That around here you never know if you'll end up like... like others who passed through.
She stops before finishing the sentence. Like she's already said more than she meant to.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Forget it. I'm just tired, that's all.
